title: Reach, leads, sales and conversion rate

sections.skill: Follow reach, leads and sales and find the weakest step

questions.domain: Foundation 11: Marketing, sales and social media
questions.prompt: What is a lead?

choices.text: A heavy metal used in old pipes
A person who never saw the message
A person who has already paid twice

questions.intro: Marketing results can be followed in steps. REACH is how many people saw your message. LEADS are people who showed interest, such as signing up or asking a question. SALES are people who paid. Each step has a CONVERSION RATE: leads / reach, and sales / leads. Example: 2,000 reached, 100 leads (5 percent), 20 sales (20 percent of leads). Finding the step where most people drop off shows what to improve: the message, the offer or the follow-up.

questions.domain: Foundation 11: Marketing, sales and social media
questions.prompt: 10 percent of 500 reached become leads. How many leads?
questions.intro: When results pass through steps, multiply the rates. If 5 percent of 2,000 people become leads, that is 0.05 x 2,000 = 100 leads. If 20 percent of leads buy, that is 0.20 x 100 = 20 sales. You can also multiply the rates first: 0.05 x 0.20 = 0.01, so 1 percent of the people reached buy: 0.01 x 2,000 = 20. Both ways give the same answer.
